quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson on the difficulty of playing alongside Giannis Antetokounmpo
quotes.excerpt: I wouldn't want to play with Giannis. He's a great player, but I don't want to be in a corner.
quotes.quote: If I'm on, I wouldn't want to play with Giannis. He's a great player, but I don't want to be in a corner shooting grenades the whole game. I love Giannis to death. I think he's one of the best players to ever play basketball, but I didn't fit with Giannis at all. Bryn Forbes played well with Giannis because he's a shooter. He was like, I'll shoot a grenade, I don't care. Even like, and not to call nobody out, but like, Jrue Holiday had a tough time. He won, we won, but it was tough for us.

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson argues that the Milwaukee Bucks' championship was team construction
quotes.excerpt: They didn't win a championship. They won with Giannis, right? They figured it out.
quotes.quote: Did they win a championship? They won with Giannis, right? They figured it out. So you can win with Giannis. Do they have a Chris Middleton? Can you win with Giannis? Chris Middleton, to me, can be a Chris Middleton? No, not the same player. To me, they are not the same players. Wiggins ain't been that guy since he came into the league. He has been a guy that is going to 3-and-D, shoot threes, and defend. That has been his role for at least five plus years now. Am I wrong? I mean, that's what I've seen. That's what we see. That's what we played in Chris Middleton, my bugging?

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson questions Erik Spoelstra's leadership during the Miami Heat's slump
quotes.excerpt: You got a guy like Spoelstra in the game three talking about inspiration. He's lost.
quotes.quote: You got a guy like Spoelstra in the game three talking about inspiration. He's lost. People are saying Bam is trash, it's crazy to me. And people are going to say that because Bam's numbers have been trash. But you can't tell me Bam has been in a great position to be successful. You can't tell me that. Now, do I think Bam should go be more aggressive? 1,000%.

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson credits Kyrie Irving's impact on the 2021 championship
quotes.excerpt: If Kyrie Irving doesn't roll his ankle, they sweep these niggas.
quotes.quote: If Kyrie Irving doesn't roll his ankle, they sweep these niggas. But he did. But he did, and they won. Okay, so we can't go there. No, we can, though. I think it's something, and you say we watch basketball. We watch basketball. If he fucking sat there and Kyrie Irving doesn't roll his ankle and James Harden doesn't have a pulled hamstring and playing on one leg, they get swept. If you ask every Milwaukee Buck player on that team in 2020, 2021, if they thought they were going to beat the Brooklyn Nets, they would all say, no. When Kyrie Irving got hurt, that's when we knew, oh fuck, we might have a fucking chance now.

quotes.speaker: Raymond Felton
quotes.summary_phrase: Raymond Felton defends Giannis Antetokounmpo's supporting cast
quotes.excerpt: He's never had the players around him. Even the championship year that they won.
quotes.quote: He's never had the players around him. Even the championship year that they won, who's their second best player? Chris Middleton. Was Chris Middleton a top 15 player in the league? No, but he was All-Star though. Okay, cool. But he was to me, 20, 25. So why did they not, why did they lose in 2023, 2024 when they had Dame? Dame was there in 2025, Giannis was there in 2030.

quotes.speaker: Theo Pinson
quotes.summary_phrase: Theo Pinson suggests Giannis Antetokounmpo needs to develop a jump shot
quotes.excerpt: What he has to do is create a jump shot. He has to go work on that.
quotes.quote: What he has to do is create a jump shot. He has to go work on that. At this age, you're not getting a jump shot. Why not? A lot of people shot better as they got older. It's a fact. You shoot better as you get older because you can't do some of the things you did when you were younger. You shoot better as you get older. I just think he needs to work on that. But seriously though, like when you're in the playoffs, you can't just bully people and go inside the paint and just do that. It's just not going to be good for the offense. But if you are a threat to hit an open jump shot, along with what you can do in the paint, I think that makes you even more dangerous.

quotes.speaker: Raymond Felton
quotes.summary_phrase: Raymond Felton emphasizes team construction around Giannis Antetokounmpo
quotes.excerpt: If Miami Heat had Kyrie Irving, if Miami Heat had a point guard, we're talking about a whole different.
quotes.quote: If Miami Heat had Kyrie Irving, if Miami Heat had a point guard, we're talking about a whole different shit. Giannis doesn't have to change his game, right? Yeah. So it's team construction around Giannis is what matters, it's not Giannis. You can win with Giannis. A part of it is what Ray just said. Your development has to elevate your team. Giannis, how many pull-up fucking middies did he shoot against Charlotte? Too many.

quotes.speaker: Raymond Felton
quotes.summary_phrase: Raymond Felton challenges the idea that Giannis makes teammates better
quotes.excerpt: He averages a triple double, and he still didn't win, and he makes people better.
quotes.quote: Who does Russell Westbrook make better? He hasn't won. I'm going by your theory, your analogy. He makes everybody better? What do you mean? But he still didn't win. He averages a triple double, and he still didn't win, and he makes people better. So he averages a triple double, he makes people better, and he doesn't win. How does that make sense? Are we, my bugging right now? Are you serious? I'm willing to bet, instead, Russell Westbrook, other than a championship, has went further in the playoffs multiple times than Giannis has. Am I wrong? With the Clippers he's went further, with Houston he's went further, with fucking OKC he's went further. But he doesn't have the one championship.
